title.narrative: Argentina Listening to the Poor for Improving the Impact of Social Policies

description.narrative: The objective of this proposal is to contribute to improve the impact of social policies on the poor by addressing Government.s efforts to improve institutional channels for interaction with civil society. Public demands for improved Government performance in the design and execution of social policies and for more profound civil society engagement in policy-making strike at the core of Argentina.s governance dilemmas. In order to promote civil society participation in the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of social policies, this IDF grant will contribute to strengthen: i) Government.s capacity to engage with grassroots organizations at the local level and ii) grassroots organizations. capacity to articulate their efforts and present their demands to Government through networks. Specifically, this IDF Grant will support CENOC in : 1. designing and piloting a methodology to train grassroots organizations -that are part of networks- nation-wide in managerial techniques, taking into account regional socio-political contexts. Networks are the most result-oriented forms of institutional linkage among CSOs. Strong networks can contribute to improve the impact of social policies by offering the poor an institutional channel to send feedback to the Government on their performance in relation to those policies and present new demands in accordance with local realities, by ensuring poor groups. capacity to access and disseminate updated information on social programs at national, provincial and local levels, by strengthening their representation in public debates, by encouraging community-driven strategies to address poor people.s development priorities, and by promoting the civic engagement of the poor. improving and updating its database of grassroots organizations and its communications network. CENOC manages the most important database of CSOs existing in the country, used as a key tool to collect information to design adequate social policies. This database currently contains information on approximately 10310 CSOs. profiles, and consulted on a daily basis by public agencies, international organizations, researchers, universities and CSOs themselves. For a CSO to be registered in this database means greater visibility and more possibilities of interacting with other institutions. But the agency.s needs to improve its deficient communication skills. These handicaps inhibit fluid contacts with organizations, specially with those located in the interior of the country. This weakness is also shared by CSOs themselves, specially grassroots organizations whose institutional capacities and possibilities of horizontal articulations have been severely impacted by the crisis. This situation has contributed to causing a mismatch between grassroots organizations requests and public responses. This IDF proposal intends to offer technical assistance to CENOC to help eradicate this gap.
